description: Hi! We're Low Battery Crew, a first-time team from Malolos, Bulacan led by a Grade 11 STEM student. We're doing "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment." No coding needed - we're telling the story of a forgotten object on the Moon/Mars through writing, research, and visuals. Perfect if you're good at writing, design, or presenting and want to finish a real project this weekend. Beginners welcome!
summary: Opportunity was sent to Mars for 90 days but lived for almost 15 years. This project is a short story tribute to Opportunity, ending with its last message: "My battery is low and it's getting dark." It reminds us that abandoned NASA equipment should not be forgotten.
details:
This project is a short story tribute for the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten."

What it does: It tells the true story of NASA's Opportunity Rover to make people care about abandoned space equipment. Instead of a technical report, we used storytelling so anyone can feel why it matters.

Intended impact: To remind the public that rovers, satellites, and landers left on other planets are part of human history and should be remembered, not just forgotten as junk.

How it is creative: We focused on Opportunity's last message - "My battery is low and it's getting dark" - and told it like a character, not a machine, so the audience connects emotionally.

Tools used: Google Docs for writing, NASA Opportunity mission page for research. Concept, story direction, and final edits by me. Drafting assistance from Meta AI.

Full story is also in the public Google Doc link above.

---

OPPORTUNITY: MY BATTERY IS LOW AND IT'S GETTING DARK

In 2004, NASA sent a small robot to Mars. Its name was Opportunity. It was supposed to live for 90 days. It lived for almost 15 years.

It survived dust storms, freezing winters, and a broken wheel. It kept driving. Scientists said good morning to it like a friend.

In June 2018, a giant dust storm covered Mars. Opportunity could not charge. Its last message was: "My battery is low and it's getting dark."

NASA tried to call it 835 times for 8 months. No answer. Opportunity is still there alone on Mars.

It was abandoned. But it should not be forgotten.
